newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products tumble, soyoil hits contract low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products tumble, soyoil hits contract low.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures tumbled to lower closes and contract lows were notched across the board in soyoil on massive fund liquidation tied to bearish technical indicators, pit sources said.
Pit sources pointed to a breakdown below $288 per ton in the July soymeal and 23.45 cent per lb in the July soyoil.

Traders said volume was thin and trade choppy ahead of the midday expiration of the May contracts. Some had expected the lack of deliveries against the May and the relatively high open interest would keep the May soymeal firm but when that contract went off the board weak, selling appeared.
"If May went off weak, they were going to sell it. If it went off firm, they were going to buy it," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soymeal ended $6.50 to $1.90 per ton lower with July off $6.50 at $285.30 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.61 to 0.04 cent per lb lower with July down 0.61 at 23.19 cents.
The new contract low for July soyoil is 23.15 cents, below the previous low of 23.60 set on Monday.
Traders cited a lack of bullish market-moving news.
"In the grain business, neutral news is bad news," one trader said. "It's got to be bullish to bring this market up."

USDA on Monday said 46 percent of the U.S. soybean crop had been seeded as of Sunday, topping the average pace of 26 percent. Traders noted early planted crops historically have produced above average yields. With USDA forecasting new crop acreage near 69 million acres, that would mean a record crop.
On the day, Merrill Lynch, Smith Barney and Dean Witter each sold at least 200 lots July soymeal. Term Commodities and Cargill Inc were also sellers.

In soyoil, commercials were buyers on the way down, led by Produce Grain with 250 lots of July purchased. ADM bought 200 July, Term Commodities bought 150 July and Cargill Inc bought 50 July and sold 250, traders said.
Iowa Grain sold at least 200 July and Refco and Dean Witter were also said to be sellers.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 29,000 lots, against Monday's actual volume of 24,925 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual of 15,327.
